conventions.convention: There are finitely many causes K ≥ 1 and finite nonnegative latent event times. The minimum is unique almost surely; the smallest minimizing label defines the cause everywhere. Latent times need not be independent.

S(t)=P(T>t), S(u−)=P(T≥u) for u>0, and S(0−)=1. Incidence and hazard integrals include [0,t]. The hazard density relative to the event subdistribution is 1/S(u−) when positive and zero otherwise; its total mass may be infinite.

An event tied with censoring is recorded as an event. Risk counts include U_i=u, all causes at a shared event time are grouped, and incidence increments use survival before the shared update. Baseline events are included, with initial survival 1 and initial incidences 0.
Fixed-time measurability uses the Borel observation space ([0,∞) × {0,1,…,K})^n, with status 0 denoting censoring and status k denoting a cause-k event, and the Borel target R^(K+1).

load_bearing.statement: F_k(t)=P(T≤t,D=k), S(t)=P(T>t), and Λ_k(B)=∫_B w(u) ν_k(du), where w(u)=1/S(u−) when S(u−)>0 and w(u)=0 otherwise.

For n≥1 records and horizon t≥0, process distinct observed event times in increasing order, grouping causes. Update F̂_k(u)=F̂_k(u−)+Ŝ(u−)ΔN_k(u)/Y(u) and Ŝ(u)=Ŝ(u−)(1−ΔN(u)/Y(u)); keep estimates constant between event times and return their values at t.

For fixed n≥1, finite K, and t≥0, the algorithm's output is a measurable map from the stated Borel observation space to R^(K+1), hence a statistic in any experiment on that space. Every event-time denominator Y(u) is positive.

For every cause k and every t≥0, F_k(t)=∫_[0,t] S(u−) dΛ_k(u). If ν_k has Lebesgue density f_k and S(u)>0 for every u∈(0,t], then Λ_k has density λ_k=f_k/S almost everywhere on (0,t], and F_k(t)=∫_0^t S(u)λ_k(u) du.

seams_checked.note: The observation definition and its uses preserve U=min(T,C), δ=1{T≤C}, and event precedence at censoring ties. No likelihood or conditional-law result is imported.

This is contextual prerequisite placement. The algorithm explicitly invokes no compensator, bracket, or process-limit result. Its grouped ties and baseline events are not claimed to satisfy the supplier's unit-jump, N_0=0 continuous-compensator contract.

The product-limit definition, inclusive endpoints, grouped event counts, and risk-set convention agree. The example faithfully applies the single-event product after recoding competing events as censorings; no consistency, variance, or asymptotic result is imported.
